correctness.rationale: Every diamond contains the apex since the rim has maximum degree two. Three rim vertices then form a two-edge path or triangle. The lower bounds n, 3, 5, and 6 follow respectively from the hub star, a rim triangle with the apex, an apex/P3 diamond, and a C3 K4 or a C4 requiring two nonspoke colors. The upper construction uses distinct consecutive spoke colors per component, a three-step modular shift on path edges, a three-step cyclic shift on cycles of length at least five, and direct distinct/alternating outside colors on C3/C4. All local diamonds and proper incidence constraints are checked in the proof. Independently, exhaustive enumerations covered 305 labeled degree<=2 graphs up to five vertices and 295 component profiles up to ten; exact backtracking checked small optimality. No finite test is substituted for the infinite argument.

value.rationale: A complete, exact, structurally natural infinite classification for cones with degree-at-most-two links. It proves the surprisingly sharp χ′_D=Δ result at all degrees >=6 for this planar subclass versus the general planar bound 2Δ−1, identifies precisely the three small-link obstructions, and supplies an explicit uniform optimal coloring even for disconnected combinations of cycles and paths. This is broader than a routine one-parameter special case or a small numerical improvement.
